modules.title: Generalization & Adaptation
modules.summary: Unseen compositions, dynamics shifts, task transfer, and adaptation.
modules.intro: World models encounter changes in object configurations, transition dynamics, observations, and goals. These papers study how learned structure transfers and how interaction history or parameter updates support adaptation.
modules.scope: Each entry specifies the tested shift and outcome. Prediction transfer, policy transfer, adaptation from context, and fine-tuning are different evaluation settings.
modules.connections:
HOWM and Dreamweaver study composition; WM3C uses language-guided causal components for unseen environments.

CaDM conditions dynamics on history, while Context and Diversity and Considering Context examine what that history reveals. Dynamics Are Learned shapes a trajectory embedding for policy adaptation.

Curious Replay changes the data used for updates; WOMBET generates source-task experience for target-task fine-tuning. Behavior-Invariant Task Representation Learning addresses changes in offline behavior and online interaction.

General agents need world models supplies a formal connection between goal generalization and prediction.

modules.title: World Model Interpretability
modules.summary: Physical variables, causal interventions, and interpretable model design.
modules.intro: Interpretability studies identify the variables represented by a world model and examine their role in prediction. Related model designs give latent variables explicit physical meaning.
modules.scope: Representation probes, interventions on model computation, behavioral tests of learned structure, and physically interpretable architectures provide different forms of evidence.
modules.connections: Interpreting Physics analyzes physical information in video representations. What Do World Models Learn in RL? extends probing and interventions to learned Atari simulators. What Has a Foundation Model Found? tests learned structure through adaptation to synthetic tasks, without identifying internal circuits. Four Principles for Physically Interpretable World Models introduces design constraints that align latent variables with physical meaning.

modules.title: Structured & Compositional Representations
modules.summary: Objects, relations, and modular transition mechanisms.
modules.intro: Object and relation structure factorizes a world model into entities and interactions. These methods infer interaction graphs, learn object-specific visual features, or restrict which components participate in a transition.
modules.scope: Structure may be supplied by the input, learned from observations, or encouraged by a prediction objective. Relation recovery and compositional transfer are reported as separate outcomes.
modules.connections: NRI infers relations between observed entities. C-SWM learns object embeddings and relational transitions from pixels. SPARTAN sparsifies context-dependent interactions to adapt to mechanism changes. Causal-JEPA makes missing object-level information the prediction target. HOWM and WM3C, listed under Generalization & Adaptation, directly evaluate how composable dynamics support new configurations or environments.

modules.title: Representation Geometry & Symmetry
modules.summary: Latent geometry, symmetry priors, and predictive dynamics.
modules.intro: Geometric structure determines how states and transitions are represented in latent space. These papers study regularization for long-horizon prediction and symmetry-based constraints on learned dynamics.
modules.scope: Observed geometry, imposed symmetry, and improved rollout accuracy are distinct claims. Physical-variable probing is covered under World Model Interpretability; language-model geometry and procedural planning appear in Supplementary Reading.
modules.connections: GRWM regularizes an encoder using geometric information and temporal context to improve deterministic rollouts. Group-Structured Latent Space specifies a symmetry-based latent manifold and transition operations. Dynamics Are Learned, listed under Generalization & Adaptation, instead shapes an inferred context embedding to support policies under dynamics shifts.

modules.title: Planning & Task-Relevant World Models
modules.summary: Goal-directed prediction, task abstraction, and model-based action selection.
modules.intro: World models support action selection through predicted futures or representations that preserve decision-relevant quantities. These papers connect latent dynamics to planning, task abstraction, and task-agnostic experience collection.
modules.scope: The evaluation target can be goal-reaching, reward, or the quantities needed for policy evaluation. Task success is interpreted in the tested environment and transfer protocol.
modules.connections: DINO-WM plans in frozen visual features; V-JEPA 2 connects video pretraining to action-conditioned prediction and robot planning. JEPA-WMs separates encoder, objective, and planner choices. Denoised MDPs isolates controllable and reward-relevant factors, while Value Equivalence formalizes the model information needed for Bellman updates. Plan2Explore collects experience through disagreement between predictors before downstream rewards are specified.

modules.title: Evaluation & Benchmarks
modules.summary: Physical extrapolation, compositional tests, and closed-loop evaluation.
modules.intro: Evaluation protocols expose failures that average prediction scores can hide. These papers test physical-law extrapolation, combinations absent from training, and action-conditioned world models used in closed-loop tasks.
modules.scope: Results depend on the training distribution, the tested change, the information available at deployment, and the measured outcome. Simulation-based policy evaluation is linked separately in Supplementary Reading.
modules.connections: A Physical Law Perspective isolates interpolation, extrapolation, and compositional physical prediction. World-In-World evaluates action-conditioned models in closed-loop tasks while varying post-training data and test-time computation. The former diagnoses prediction under distribution shift; the latter measures consequences for interaction.

groups.title: World-model foundations
groups.intro: Predictive architectures and model-based RL baselines for implementing representation and planning studies.

groups.title: Related representation methods
groups.intro: Geometry and analysis methods from language modeling and procedural planning, with their original evaluation domains retained.

groups.title: Simulation, transfer, and system identification
groups.intro: Adjacent studies of policy evaluation, simulator calibration, and task-informed interaction.

route.label: Interpreting Physics
route.connection: Introduces probes and interventions for physical information in representations; the next paper applies related tools to learned environment simulators.

route.label: Probing RL World Models
route.connection: Connects decodable state variables to generated predictions through interventions, complementing the video-representation analysis in the first paper.

route.label: What Has a Foundation Model Found?
route.connection: Tests learned structure through behavior on new tasks, providing a different form of evidence from inspecting internal activations.

route.label: HOWM
route.connection: Formalizes object composition as a generalization problem, giving an explicit target for reusable dynamics.

route.label: WM3C
route.connection: Connects compositional modeling to language-guided causal factors and adaptation in unseen tasks.

route.label: Group-Structured Latent Space
route.connection: Introduces known symmetries as a structural prior, contrasting with factors inferred through object composition or language.

route.label: GRWM
route.connection: Examines geometric regularization and prediction error, complementing the explicit symmetry constraints in the preceding paper.

route.label: Context and Diversity Matter
route.connection: Shifts the focus from representation design to the information supplied by experience in a new environment.

route.label: Dynamics Are Learned, Not Told
route.connection: Connects representation geometry to dynamics adaptation through embeddings inferred from trajectories.

route.label: WOMBET
route.connection: Adds parameter-updating transfer through model-generated experience, alongside the preceding context-based adaptation mechanisms.

route.label: DINO-WM
route.connection: Connects latent prediction to action optimization and goal-reaching, making downstream use of the representation explicit.

route.label: A Physical Law Perspective
route.connection: Examines failures under physical extrapolation and composition, distinguishing successful prediction within a distribution from transfer beyond it.

route_sections.intro: Object composition, causal components, and symmetry priors as ways to organize reusable dynamics.

route_sections.title: 07–09 · Geometry and adaptation
route_sections.intro: Geometric regularization, learning from context, and representations of changing dynamics.

route_sections.title: 10–12 · Transfer, planning, and evaluation
route_sections.intro: Model-generated experience, latent-space planning, and physical generalization tests.
